fixes.why: The sentence gives Lutheran teaching only its falling-away half. It leaves out the Lutheran account of return and of assurance, which the _why says was omitted so as not to favour reading 2. Assurance rests on the promise, and a Lutheran reader would not sign the sentence as it stands.
fixes.fix: Replace 'Lutheran teaching holds that a believer can fall from faith and that God keeps believers in faith through his word and sacraments; Lutheran readers differ from Reformed readers here.' with 'Lutheran teaching holds that a believer can fall from faith, that God keeps believers in faith through his word and sacraments, and that a person who has fallen away is brought back by the word of forgiveness; Lutheran readers take assurance to rest on the promise of that word, and differ from Reformed readers on whether the elect can fall.'

fixes.why: The note lists what assurance may rest on but omits the Catholic position that no one may hold with the certainty of faith that he will persevere to the end, apart from special revelation. A Catholic reader would find the assurance term incomplete on the question this card asks.
fixes.fix: Append to the assurance note: ' The Catholic teaching is that no one may hold with the certainty of faith that he will persevere to the end, apart from a special revelation.'

fixes.why: The sentence names faithfulness as part of following Christ but does not say what Anabaptist readers hold about the warnings, so the tradition is credited with the falling-away reading without its own position on it.
fixes.fix: Replace 'Anabaptist readers speak of faithfulness to the end as part of following Christ.' with 'Anabaptist readers hold that the warnings are addressed to the gathered church of believers, and that a disciple who turns from following Christ can fall away; they speak of faithfulness to the end as part of that following.'

fixes.why: General and Free Will Baptist churches hold the falling-away reading, but the card places the Baptist line only in readings 2 and 3, so a Baptist reader sees their own diversity left out. The held_by list and the summary should show it, and it is accurate for this reading.
fixes.fix: Add 'Baptist / free church' to reading 1 held_by. After the Wesleyan sentence in the summary, add: 'General and Free Will Baptist readers hold this reading, and differ from the Baptist readers below on whether a believer can fall away.'

fixes.why: The label makes a popular slogan the name of the reading, and the summary calls the slogan 'the phrase in popular use', which sets it against the theology as a casual form. Conservative Baptist readers would take this as dismissive of their own term, and a reader outside the US mainstream would see the slogan as a US idiom standing in for the doctrine.
fixes.fix: Label: 'Eternal security: eternal life is given when a person believes and rests on Christ's work and God's faithfulness, so it is not lost'. In the summary replace 'and “once saved, always saved” is the phrase in popular use for it.' with 'and many of its holders use the phrase “once saved, always saved” for it.' Keep the term entry as it is.

fixes.why: The note reads Ezekiel as 'a pattern the New Testament warnings continue', a link the holders of this reading are not recorded as making, and it stops at 18:24 although the same chapter gives the turning wicked his life. Ezekiel 18 is about each person answering for his own turning; a rabbi reader would object to a verse read out of that chapter as settling a Christian debate.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'Read for the chapter's principle that each person answers for his own turning. Holders of this reading are not recorded as citing the chapter for it; the same chapter says: "But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life." (18:27)'

fixes.why: The verse is a promise to Israel and Judah in its own chapter, and the note gives the Reformed use of it without saying it is their reading, which rule 8 requires for an Old Testament verse. A Reformed reader would be glad to see it named as their use; a rabbi would see the chapter's first audience kept in view.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'A promise to Israel and Judah in its own chapter. Reformed holders cite it as God's everlasting covenant with his people, and that is their reading.'

fixes.why: The synergy term and the Orthodox and Catholic summaries rest on the will cooperating with grace, and no verse on the card states that. Philippians 2:12 is among the verses those holders cite first, and reading 1 has none of its own. Its absence would tilt reading 1 toward the verses that speak of a believer's turning and away from the verses about working out salvation.
fixes.fix: Add {"ref": "Philippians 2:12", "quote": "continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.", "note": "Believers told to continue working out their own salvation with fear and trembling."}. To keep eight passages, remove the Colossians 1:23 entry from reading 1; its answer in readings 2 and 3 can keep naming it.

summary: The card quotes every verse exactly and holds no verdict, and its three readings are fairly stated for most of the seats. The fixes are the Lutheran and Anabaptist sentences in reading 1, the missing Philippians 2:12 for the falling-away reading, the Ezekiel and Jeremiah notes for the rabbi and Reformed seats, and the Baptist and assurance wording.
